answer: In an agent marketplace trading saffron, reef surveys, and knoll maps, each seller must lock a fixed bond for 30 days to activate one bidding slot. The bond remains locked until 30 days after that slot closes. Creating names is free, but operating 1,000 fake sellers requires 1,000 bonds held simultaneously; splitting one balance cannot multiply access. This makes a sybil swarm costly in capital and prevents attackers from recycling one bond rapidly across identities.
